text.p: Tourism-related firm Boulevard Properties Holdings Inc debuted poorly on Monday after last-minute questions over its sources of capital and worries over a possible property market slump, officials said.
Boulevard shares closed at 81 centavos, compared with the offering price of one peso, on modest turnover. It reached a low of 78 centavos in midsession.

The Presidential Commission on Good Government (PCGG) last Thursday opposed the listing of Boulevard, saying it sourced 250 million pesos of its equity from advances by companies whose funds came from sequestered companies.
The PCGG is the custodian of all sequestered assets of former strongman Ferdinand Marcos and his business associates.

"I believe there's a slight effect. But this is just temporary," Boulevard vice-chairman Lorenzo Tanada told Reuters when asked how the PCGG's petition against the listing affected the first day of trading.

"The public should look at us on how we stand based on our financials, not on perceived notions that our company is using funds from, what has not been proven up to this point, crony money," Tanada said.
